record.original_question: Let F be a holomorphic foliation on the unit polydisc Dk ⊂ Ck whose leaves have dimension d > 1 and are tangent to holomorphic (1,0)-forms α1, ..., α_{k-d} that satisfy the Frobenius condition ∂α_j = Σ_{l=1}^{k-d} α_l ∧ β_{j,l}. Can F always be approximated by foliations on Ck or Pk? More precisely, can the forms α_j be approximated uniformly on compact subsets of Dk by entire forms, or by polynomial forms, that still satisfy the same Frobenius condition?

evidence.quote: Let F be a holomorphic foliation in the unit polydisc Dk in Ck. Assume that the leaves of F are of dimension d with d > 1. More precisely, the leaves of F are tangent to a family of k − d holomorphic (1, 0)-forms (αj)1≤j≤k−d on Ck.
These forms αj are linearly independent at a generic point of Dk and satisfy the Frobenius condition ∂αj = Σk−d l=1 αl ∧ βj,l with j = 1, . . . , k − d for some holomorphic (1, 0)-forms βj,l in Dk.

Problem 11.1. Is it always possible to approximate the foliation F by foliations in Ck or Pk ? More precisely, is it always possible to approximate the forms αj, uniformly on compact sets of Dk, by entire forms (resp. polynomial forms) αj,n which still satisfy the above Frobenius condition ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}^k \subset \mathbb{C}^k$ denote the open unit polydisc, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a holomorphic foliation on $\mathbb{D}^k$ whose leaves have complex dimension $d$ with $d>1$. Assume $\mathcal{F}$ is given by $k-d$ holomorphic $(1,0)$-forms $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{k-d}$ on $\mathbb{D}^k$ that are linearly independent at a generic point and satisfy the Frobenius integrability condition
$$\partial \alpha_j = \sum_{l=1}^{k-d} \alpha_l \wedge \beta_{j,l}, \qquad j=1,\dots,k-d,$$
for some holomorphic $(1,0)$-forms $\beta_{j,l}$ on $\mathbb{D}^k$.

Question: Can each $\alpha_j$ be approximated, uniformly on every compact subset of $\mathbb{D}^k$, by holomorphic $(1,0)$-forms $\alpha_{j,n}$ defined on all of $\mathbb{C}^k$ (respectively, by polynomial $(1,0)$-forms, viewed as forms on $\mathbb{P}^k$) such that, for each $n$, the approximating forms $\alpha_{1,n},\dots,\alpha_{k-d,n}$ themselves satisfy a Frobenius condition
$$\partial \alpha_{j,n} = \sum_{l=1}^{k-d} \alpha_{l,n} \wedge \beta_{j,l,n}$$
for some holomorphic (respectively polynomial) $(1,0)$-forms $\beta_{j,l,n}$? Equivalently, can every such foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{D}^k$ be approximated by holomorphic foliations on $\mathbb{C}^k$ or $\mathbb{P}^k$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this Runge-type approximation problem for holomorphic foliations of leaf dimension $d>1$ on the polydisc. Standard Runge/Oka–Weil approximation results apply to holomorphic functions and forms on polydiscs, but preserving the Frobenius integrability condition under approximation is a nontrivial constraint, and no source found explicitly settles the question.

status_evidence.title: Holomorphic approximation: the legacy of Weierstrass, Runge, Oka–Weil, and Mergelyan
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of holomorphic approximation; discusses approximation on polydiscs and Stein manifolds but does not resolve Frobenius-preserving approximation for foliations of leaf dimension >1.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution of the Frobenius-preserving approximation question is reported in this comprehensive survey of holomorphic approximation.

status_evidence.title: A Runge Approximation Theorem for Pseudo-Holomorphic Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Runge-type approximation results in related settings.
status_evidence.claim: Related Runge-type theorems exist but do not address the specific Frobenius-integrable foliation approximation problem.
